problems.title: Marginal transport improvement does not establish semantic gain
claim: The theorem chains input information bounds into a claimed semantic-information improvement from marginal Wasserstein alignment.
analysis: Let independent fair bits \(C,U\) form \(X=Y=(C,U)\), and \(Z=U\oplus E\) with independent crossover \(E\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\). A decoder reading only the nuisance bit has positive probabilities and globally Lipschitz negative log probabilities after clipped linear extension. Equal marginals give optimal transport reduction \(\Delta=0\). Yet \(I(Z;C)=0\), \(I(Z;X,Y)=r=\log2-h(1/4)>0\), and admissible residual bound \(\varepsilon=r\) makes the printed chain \(0\ge0\ge r\), false. Independently, let \(X=C\) be a fair bit, \(Y=0\), and decoder probability \(q(Z=1\mid x)=1/4+x/2\). Optimal transport maps \(X\) to zero, reducing Wasserstein distance \(1/\sqrt2\to0\), but the rerun encoder’s task information drops \(r\to0\). Regularity holds and no task-sufficiency premise excludes this.
result: The chain omits a necessary residual term, and even restoring it does not prove that marginal alignment preserves or improves semantics. Transport can remain an empirically useful heuristic.
repair: For \(W=(T(X),Y)\) and \(C\to W\to Z_T\), the valid identity is \(I(Z_T;C)=I(Z_T;W)-I(Z_T;W\mid C)\). An upper residual bound gives its corresponding lower bound only; a transport-gain theorem needs task-sufficiency and joint-law control.
problems.impact_rationale: The central theoretical bridge used to replace unavailable semantic supervision fails on admissible regular models, beyond the isolated missing residual term.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: The Gaussian information bound lacks its real-valued domain
claim: The bound contains \(-\log(1-\operatorname{Var}(\mu_i)/\sigma_i^2)\) without requiring the ratio below one.
analysis: Choose independent \(\mu\sim N(0,2)\), \(R=\epsilon\sim N(0,1)\), \(\sigma=1\). The joint covariance is positive definite, its normalized cross-covariance matrix is zero and satisfies the stated diagonal domination, but the ratio is \(2\). Actual information is zero, while the printed real logarithm is \(\log(-1)\). Also \(M\preceq\operatorname{diag}(M_{ii})\) forces exact diagonality, since their positive-semidefinite difference has zero trace. Independent encoder noise plus joint Gaussianity makes zero covariance imply independence; heteroscedastic non-Gaussian encoders need not satisfy that idealization.
result: A missing positivity restriction makes the formula undefined on its claimed domain. No real-valued too-small bound or actual learned-encoder violation is asserted.
repair: Require \(0\preceq M\preceq D\prec I\) and ratios \(r_i<1\). Gaussian information \(-\log\det(I-M)/2\) and determinant monotonicity then give the restricted logarithmic bound; ratios at least one require an explicit vacuous convention.
problems.impact_rationale: The domain omission has a direct restricted correction and does not show the actual encoder’s information decomposition fails.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Training and evaluation feed different modality order to one encoder
claim: The dataset returns visible then infrared; training aligns infrared and passes aligned-infrared then visible, while evaluation forwards the original order without alignment.
analysis: For constant visible \(1\) and infrared \(0\), balanced transport helper \(.8(PY)+.2X\) yields aligned infrared \(.8\). Encoder inputs become \((.8,1)\) in training and \((1,0)\) at evaluation. An allowed first convolution selecting its second channel gives outputs \(1\) and \(0\), proving no architectural equivalence. The later decoder cannot retroactively change encoded skip features. Omitting alignment appears in inference pseudocode and may be deliberate; the channel reversal is an additional discrepancy.
result: Current source paths supply materially different conditioning to the same unconstrained encoder. No checkpoint quality change is quantified.
repair: Define one intended modality order/preprocessing path and identify the path used by experimental checkpoints before evaluating a correction.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release correspondence defect, without reproduced empirical damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Universal superiority exceeds the reported metric tables
problems.source_location: Quantitative comparison tables and corresponding discussion
claim: The text extends superiority to all fusion metrics.
analysis: The published headers specify metric directions. On MFNet, HCLFuse is best in only \(5\) of \(12\) displayed metrics including ties; for example CC \(0.5454\) is below DDFM \(0.6082\), and PIQE \(24.135\) is worse than CCF \(20.218\), where smaller is better. On FMB it is best in \(8\) of \(12\). The segmentation mean \(89.72\) is consistent with its displayed class averages, a retained positive control.
result: Metric-specific trade-offs contradict a universal ordering, without disputing the table measurements.
repair: Describe superiority only on the supported metrics and retain competing strengths.
problems.impact_rationale: The issue is a local interpretation overreach, not a false empirical measurement.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Averaging does not establish statistical significance
claim: The checklist infers statistical significance from averaging many dataset tests.
analysis: For \(1000\) paired bounded scores, take baseline \(.5\) throughout and method scores \(.601\) on half and \(.401\) on half. Mean gain is \(.001\), but exactly half the differences are positive, giving two-sided sign-test \(p=1\); the paired t statistic is about \(.316\). Thus many averaged observations do not by themselves prove significance. This example is a logical diagnostic, not the paper’s scores.
result: Actual significance remains undetermined without raw paired data and a valid inferential design.
repair: Keep the descriptive means or supply paired uncertainty/testing aligned to independent scene/sequence units and checkpoint variation.
problems.impact_rationale: This corrects the checklist’s inference, without establishing that any specific reported improvement is nonsignificant.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Major: the central surrogate justification from marginal alignment to semantic information is invalid; the method’s empirical usefulness is not negated.
